content: hi everyone! i'm working on https://theorems.fun, a bounty website for Lean theorems. the idea is to financially incentivize the solving of lean problems. the site is still very much under development, but i'd consider this v0.1, any comments would be very much welcome!
i'm not familiar with zero knowledege proofs outside of cryptography - say more?
Maybe this is related to evariste's question: How do you prevent MEV searchers from frontrunning bounty claims?

The instructions say "Fill in your theorem HEADER only. You MUST start with 'theorem' and end with ':='.". Is there any way for me to place a bounty on a theorem that includes definitions I have made?
It says my theorem is rejected "Theorem header must end with ':='" but my submission does end with :=
(I tried again just now and got it to work, perhaps the issue is that I initially didn't put a title?)
I don't understand the crypto space well, recently also saw https://www.demath.org/ how do they compare to this?

I think this is a very nice and original idea, I just hope you can advertise it well enough to people so that it can take off. I assume you use some smart contract or some way to wire USDC to cryptowallets which was fun to see. It will be particularly interested to see how AI agents would fair on this platform against humans.
